title: Primarily static circuit design strategy
decision: Adopt a predominantly static-circuit design strategy, with dynamic circuits used only sparingly in SRAMs and other critical regions of the processor core.
rationale: Power dissipation was a significant concern, and it was a key factor; SOI technology uncertainties associated with the floating-body effect and its impact on noise immunity and decoupling capacitance; size and logical complexity of the chip posed risks to meeting the schedule; choosing a simple, robust circuit style helped to minimize overall risk.
outcome: Complementary static circuits were used predominantly; dynamic circuits limited to some register files, array circuitry, and some load/store unit circuitry.
quote_as_recalled: These constraints led to the adoption of a primarily static-circuit design strategy, with dynamic circuits used only sparingly in SRAMs and other critical regions of the processor core.
weakest_point: Exact page number and whether any specific dynamic alternatives were explicitly rejected beyond 'sparingly'

title: Single chip-wide global clock domain without skew feedback
decision: Use a single chip-wide global clock domain with no skew feedback or adjustment settings, driven by one centrally placed PLL, with buffered H-trees to 64 sector buffers driving tunable sector trees into a single full-chip clock grid.
rationale: Simple clock timing and rapid bring-up; primary goals of minimum clock uncertainty margin and timing simplicity; resulting modeled skew was negligible so clock timing consisted only of an uncertainty due to model and process errors assumed identical for each of the 15200 global clock pins.
outcome: Measured jitter of 35 ps and skew of 20 ps; ability to neglect modeled skew and use a simple constant clock uncertainty contributed to rapid chip-timing progress; correct-by-design methodology without feedback or adjustment circuitry.
quote_as_recalled: Simple clock timing and rapid bring-up were facilitated by using a single chip-wide global clock domain with no skew feedback or adjustment settings.
weakest_point: Exact wording of the full multi-sentence rationale cluster

title: Global signal slew-rate limit of one-third cycle time
decision: Set and enforce a global slew rate limit equal to one third of the cycle time for all signals (local and global) across the whole chip.
rationale: Ensure a robust design, minimizing the effects of coupled noise on chip timing and also minimizing the effects of wiring-process variability on overall path delay; nets with poor slew more sensitive to device process variations and modeling uncertainties; chip cycle-time goals also had to include the slew-limit targets.
outcome: Approximately 100000 buffers and inverters added to maintain slew rates; real hardware would function at desired cycle time only if slew-limit targets also met.
quote_as_recalled: A global slew rate limit equal to one third of the cycle time was set and enforced for all signals (local and global) across the whole chip.
weakest_point: Precise count of added buffers as reported outcome

title: Fourteen-wiring-track power-grid image for common-mode noise control
decision: Adopt a fourteen-wiring-track image for the power grid (four tracks to power/ground, ten to signal), after redesigning rectangular metal C4 pads, instead of the prior wide power/ground buses repeated at wide intervals.
alternatives_or_rejected: Typical prior IBM microprocessor power-distribution design of wide power/ground buses repeated along C4 rows (and relatively wide lower-level buses) which satisfied dc but not common-mode noise requirements.
rationale: Early circuit analyses showed the prior design point would not satisfy common-mode noise requirements (<200 mV for worst-case wide-bus activity); solution was to use more power buses to reduce return-path inductance and resistance, creating more quiet wiring tracks.
outcome: Power grid that came closest to meeting dc-noise, common-mode-noise, quiet-wiring-track, and wirability requirements; exceptions allowed if power/ground at least 25% of tracks and no more than ten signal wires between power buses.
quote_as_recalled: the power grid that came closest to meeting the dc-noise, common-mode-noise, quiet-wiring-track, and wirability requirements was a fourteen-wiring-track image.
weakest_point: Exact page and whether 250 nF or 300 nF decoupling is the final reported figure

title: Hierarchical four-level design methodology with contracts for concurrent work
decision: Organize the chip physically and logically in a four-level hierarchy (macro, unit, core, chip) with contracts (early size and timing budgets) enabling concurrent design across levels and separation of logic entry/simulation from circuit design/floorplanning/timing.
rationale: Facilitates concurrent design across all four levels; provided that the proper contracts have been created, all of this work can proceed independently and in parallel; further parallelism by separating logic entry and simulation from circuit design, floorplanning, and timing.
outcome: At completion of high-level design, consistent contracts in place across all levels; design progressed through high-level, schematic, and physical phases with increasing refinement; multi-site team synchronized via Common Tools Environment.
quote_as_recalled: This hierarchy facilitates concurrent design across all four levels.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames this as a weighed decision versus a pure description of the adopted methodology
